subject: POC Success Criteria & KPIs — AveryPay trial plan
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@averypay.com>, Priya Rao <priya@averypay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-02T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: POC Success Criteria & KPIs — AveryPay trial plan

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for the demo and the candid discussion today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment before the kickoff: 

Call recap (high level):
- Goal: Evaluate Redwood inference for customer support automation and transaction classification at AveryPay scale.
- Primary constraints: low-latency scoring at peak (fast UX), predictable unit cost, and extraction accuracy on 4 key fields.
- Internal owners: Samir (CTO) and Priya (PM) on AveryPay side; Jordan (AE) + Marissa (CS) + Evelyn (SRE) on Redwood side.

Proposed POC scope & success criteria (draft):
1) Latency: P50 < 200ms, P95 < 500ms for 512-token average request paths
2) Throughput: sustain 200 requests/sec during 1-hour soak with 5% allowed error budget
3) Cost: target cost/token <= $0.0005 (aggregate across requests; we will show granular token-level breakdown)
4) Quality: extraction accuracy >= 92% on a validation set of ~1,000 labeled examples; manually review sample of 200 for edge cases

Evaluation plan (draft):
- Redwood provides a staging endpoint + exportable logs. AveryPay provides a labeled eval set (we can start with 1,000 samples) and a small production trace for latency/throughput testing.
- We will run a 4-week POC: Week 0 - kickoff & infra setup; Week 1-2 - integration + ramp tests; Week 3 - evaluation and iterative tuning; Week 4 - final validation and decision.

Attachments: Redwood POC template (attached) — includes checklist, telemetry we will collect, and the evaluation matrix.

Next steps: 
- Can you confirm the owners and the 1,000-sample eval set availability?
- Proposed kickoff window: Mon 2026-03-09 or Tue 2026-03-10 (30–45 min).

I’ll loop in Marissa and Evelyn to start scheduling and prep. Thanks — excited to get this running.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.ai]

Cc: Priya Rao <priya@averypay.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC Success Criteria & KPIs — AveryPay trial plan

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear recap. Confirming owners: Priya (PM) will own evaluation coordination and provide the labeled set; I (Samir) will own infra decisions and sign-off. The proposed POC timeline looks good — 4 weeks is reasonable.

A few clarifications / tweaks to the success criteria from our side:
- Latency: we care most about user-facing paths (average request length ~420 tokens). Can we commit to reporting P50/P95 for both 420-token and 512-token slices?
- Throughput: we need to validate sustained 200 req/s, but will also test a 600 req/s short burst for peak tolerance (30s).
- Cost: baseline target $0.0005/token is acceptable as a target; we need to see cost at both quantized and non-quantized model settings.
- Quality: instead of a single accuracy metric, we want: extraction precision >= 93% and recall >= 90% on the 1,000-sample eval set. Additionally, we’ll run a qualitative review of 200 edge cases.

We attached our initial evaluation plan (AveryPay_evaluation_plan.xlsx) with sample selection criteria and a proposed 1,000-sample split.

Questions for Redwood:
1) Who will be the single point of contact for infra/setup (we need someone to own Docker/K8s onboarding and the staging endpoint)?
2) What telemetry will you need from our side beyond the labeled set and a short production trace?

If that all sounds good, Priya and I can finalize the kickoff time. Thanks — looking forward.

Best,
Samir Gupta
CTO, AveryPay

Date: 2026-03-03T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC Success Criteria & KPIs — AveryPay trial plan

Thanks Samir — this is super helpful. Confirming on our side: 

- Single POC infra/contact: Marissa Cole will own onboarding and infra coordination (K8s/Docker staging endpoint + keys). She will work with Evelyn on runtime configuration and telemetry. I’ll remain the commercial lead and will own the success criteria alignment and sign-off process.

- Telemetry we’ll collect (initial list):
  * Per-request latency (P50/P90/P95), token counts, model variant used
  * Per-batch throughput and error rates
  * Token-level cost breakdown and per-request cost
  * Extraction precision/recall on provided labeled set + sample ID mapping for manual review
  * System metrics: GPU utilization, mem, tail latency traces during soak tests

Updated plan & timeline (proposed):
- Week 0 (Kickoff, M-0): Kickoff call, access provisioning, exchange sample traces and the 1,000 labeled examples.
- Week 1: Integration & basic smoke tests; smallest model variant to validate inference path.
- Week 2: Load/soak tests to validate throughput & latency targets; run burst tests (600 req/s for 30s).
- Week 3: Run full eval on labeled set; compute precision/recall and perform 200-case manual review.
- Week 4: Tuning, final validation, and decision review.

Deliverables from Redwood: POC checklist (attached), daily test reports during soak, a post-POC report with telemetry + cost analysis + recommended configuration for production.

Proposed kickoff times (all PT): Mon 2026-03-09 10:00, Tue 2026-03-10 11:00, or Wed 2026-03-11 09:00. Please confirm which works for your team.

Next steps for Samir/Priya: confirm kickoff slot and share the labeled dataset link (or a sample). For our part, Marissa will initiate infra prep after kickoff.

Thanks — looping Marissa and Evelyn to start the operational checklist.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
